lesson.title: AI-powered scams
lesson.subtitle: What AI changes about scams, and the habits that still beat them

video.title: AI-powered scams
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria, the student's teacher (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher, the student's teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talking to the student)

scenes.visual: Cards: Mum's voice?; “Send airtime, quickly!”; A copied voice.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: My nephew got a voice note last month. It was his mum's voice, worried: “I've lost my phone, send airtime to this new number, quickly!” It wasn't her: it was a copy of her voice, made from a video she had posted.

scenes.visual: The title card: the course, the lesson title and subtitle, the Darsi mark.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: how AI makes scams more convincing, and the habits that still beat them.

scenes.visual: Two columns. Still works: A rush or a threat; Asks for a code; A strange link. Fails now: Bad spelling; A strange voice.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: You already know the old signs of a scam: a rush, a prize, a strange link, bad spelling. AI changes some of them. It writes perfect messages in any language. And it can copy a voice or a face from what people post.

scenes.visual: A table: what Tunde shared online beside what a scam message from “Coach Ali (new number)” says with it; the last row, a request for his code, lights up.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Scammers also use what you share. Your school, your friends' names, your team: AI can mix them into a message that feels personal. But a message that knows you is not proof it comes from someone you know.

scenes.visual: A list: “Free premium” copies; Steal logins, read messages; Official store only; Check the maker and access.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Then there are fake AI apps, like “free premium” chatbots. Some steal your login or read your messages. Get apps only from the official store, and check who made them and what they ask for.

scenes.visual: A sequence diagram: a copied voice asks you for airtime; you call the saved number; the real person answers “That wasn't me!”; a note: or ask what only they'd know.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The best defence doesn't depend on spotting the fake. It's a habit: verify on a second channel. Hang up, and call back on the number you already have. Or ask something only the real person would know.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A message from your best friend's number says: “Send me the six-digit code you just got, it's for the game.” What do you do?

scenes.visual: A list: Nobody should ask for it; Friends' accounts get taken over; Check another way.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Don't send it. A code is a key, and nobody should ask for it. Your friend's account may have been taken over, so check another way.

scenes.visual: Cards: Agree a word; Never posted online; A call asks for money?; Ask for the word.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: For copied voices, agree a family code word, never posted online. If a call or voice note asks for money in a hurry, ask for the word. A copied voice can't know it.

scenes.visual: Cards joined by arrows: A stranger calls; Authority, hurry, fear; Refuse; Safe.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, a stranger calls you during break and asks for your code. Answer the way many people would, and see how fast it goes wrong. Then take the call again, refuse, and spot each trick he uses.

scenes.visual: A list: Tell an adult; Change your password; Call the bank or agent; Act fast.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: What if you were tricked? Don't hide it: tell an adult, change your password, and call the bank or mobile money agent straight away. The sooner you act, the more you can save.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A voice note sounds exactly like your uncle: he's stuck and needs mobile money now. What's your first move?

scenes.visual: The summary: Voices can be copied; Never share codes; Official stores only; Verify on a second channel. Takeaway: A real person can always wait while you check.
scenes.animation: Points tick in as they are said; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: Call his usual number, or ask for the code word, because a voice can be copied. Remember: codes are keys, so never share them. Get apps from the official store. And verify on a second channel.

scenes.visual: A list: Agree a family code word; Never post it; Check your apps; Delete the strange ones.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: agree a family code word at home, and never post it. Then check the apps on your phone, or a family phone with its owner. Delete any you don't recognise, or that ask for far too much.

checkpoints.prompt: A message from your best friend's number asks for the six-digit code you just got, “for the game”. What do you do?

options.text: Send it: it's my friend's number
Don't send it, and check with my friend another way
Send only half of the code

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Right: a code is a key, and your friend's account may have been taken over.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: a code is a key to your account. Never send it; check with your friend another way.

checkpoints.prompt: A voice note sounds exactly like your uncle: he's stuck and needs mobile money now. What's your first move?

options.text: Send the money: it's his voice
Call him on his usual number, or ask for the family code word
Reply in the chat and ask him to prove it

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Yes: a voice can be copied, but it can't know your code word, and it can't answer his real number.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: a voice can be copied, and a scammer can answer in the same chat. Use a second channel.
